### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274`.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **58** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a50cd2088765218e2771326af4f393186a637dcb` — the merge of head `805709420a999120f7572d0bcd84a627c6540356` into base `e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a50cd2088765218e2771326af4f393186a637dcb && git checkout a50cd2088765218e2771326af4f393186a637dcb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274 805709420a999120f7572d0bcd84a627c6540356 && git checkout -B drift-repro e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274 && git merge --no-ff 805709420a999120f7572d0bcd84a627c6540356

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e35cf03556600d8dc4f065575fe40aeeade84274` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：开启了登录安全策略（密码过期、强制多因素、管理员要求改密码）时，每个已登录请求少查一次数据库里的会话和用户，接口更快；在远程数据库上尤其明显。
- 为什么做：以前同一个请求里，身份识别查了一次会话，安全策略检查又查一遍。
- 出错会怎样：若判断出错，可能让本该被策略拦下的用户通过；测试确认被策略拦住的用户仍然被拒、匿名和已撤销的会话照旧被拒、并发请求互不串号。
- 要你做什么：无。区域补一条认领说明后自行落地。
- 席位意见：复用的是同一次读取得出的同一结论，拦截结果不变，证据充分，可以落地。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT, with one required item before queueing** · head `805709420a999120f7572d0bcd84a627c6540356` · Part of #35457 · 2026-11-19T17:41Z · reviewed to `pm-dispatch` text at `origin/main` `fca72dfa32`

**Readings, my own.**
- `check-governed-merges --pr 35598`: 0 of 10 paths governed.
- `merge-tree` against main: clean. K=9.
- CI: 57 success / 11 skipped / 0 failed. +413/−22.
- The claim (7014672736, 16:07Z) is p1 and within the p1-only rule.

**The auth gate, read closely: the posture is the same value, not a new one.**
- **The identity step.** `resolveAuthzContext`'s session arm (`resolve-authz-context.ts:681-697`) sets `credential = 'session'` and `authGate = normalizeAuthGate(sessionData.user)` off the read that admitted the user. `resolveRequestExecutionContext` hands `{ credential, authGate }` to `onAdmission` (`request-execution-context.ts:294`). The old gate computed `evaluateAuthGate(session.user)` = `normalizeAuthGate(session.user)` + allow-list off its own second read. Same function, same input shape, one read earlier in the same request.
- **`sessionAdmittedPrincipal`** answers only when all of these hold:
  - `admittingCredentialKind` is `'session'`, so an OAuth token (`oauthScopes`) and an API key are excluded;
  - the envelope carries a non-empty `userId`.

  A forward agent gets no `onAdmission` (`resolve-execution-context.ts:299`). The helper reads only the per-request object it is handed.
- **`enforceAuthGate`.** With an admitted session it now calls `evaluateAuthGate(admitted, path, method)`. `normalizeAuthGate` reads `.authGate` and re-validates the already-normalized posture, so the allow-list and the 403 code are unchanged.
- **Fall-through.** Every other caller falls through to the old read. That includes an identity step whose session read threw: `readSession` catches it and degrades to anonymous, so no admission is recorded. The decision-2B outage (503 on a failing read) is therefore preserved where a read is still made, and where none is made the read already succeeded.
- **The declared-endpoint fallback (`dispatcher-plugin.ts`).** `resolvePrincipalId` and `readGatedSessionUser` take the same admitted principal. The probe-inactive arm still answers `undefined` before anything is read.

**Pins (names grepped).**
- `http-dispatcher.session-read-once.pin.test.ts`, on a real kernel with the gate active:
  - precondition;
  - one `sys_session` and one user read;
  - CONTROL: a held session is still refused at the gate with its code;
  - CONTROL: anonymous reads no session row;
  - CONTROL: concurrent tokens each get their own answer;
  - CONTROL: a revoked session is a 401.
- The endpoint-fallback integration describe:
  - one read for a signed-in caller;
  - CONTROL: held → 403 with its code;
  - CONTROL: anonymous → 401;
  - CONTROL: concurrent sessions are separate.
- `auth-gate-outage.pin` CASE 2 is honestly split:
  - a caller the identity step did not admit still costs exactly one extra read when the gate is active;
  - an admitted session costs none.

  The outage cases are unchanged.

**R1 (required before queueing): amend the claim for `packages/core`.** `packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts` (the door table's `authGate` row) and `assemble-execution-context.ts` (the field doc) are comment-only edits outside the claim's surface. The PR body names them with the reason at line 35: the comments said the dispatcher re-reads the session, which is no longer true. `l1-review-checklist.md` asks for both, so post a claim amendment on #35457 naming the two files. This is text only.

**Declaration: agreed.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` / runtime patch. Which requests are admitted or refused, and with which status, is unchanged, as measured by the CONTROLs. Changeset sentences checked against the diff:
- "one fewer pair of database round trips", with a gate active, on the dispatcher and the declared endpoint;
- "read once and shared between identity resolution and the authentication-policy gate";
- "admitted or refused … does not change".

"Part of" is right: the limiter and REST halves are #35606, and the REST double read is in the body's acceptance notes.

**Routing.** Not governed and no contract face. ux-3 lands it after R1.
